# Review CHANGES REQUESTED for PAN-5165

# Review — PAN-5165
## Verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED — new import cycle through `launch-pack-mcp.ts` fails `npm run lint:circular` (NFR-5) and CI `lint-group (core)`

## Context
- Run ID: agent-pan-5165-review-e88c4b58
- Manifest: /home/eltmon/Projects/overdeck/workspaces/feature-pan-5165/.pan/review/agent-pan-5165-review-e88c4b58/context.json
- Branch / workspace: feature/pan-5165 / /home/eltmon/Projects/overdeck/workspaces/feature-pan-5165
- PR: https://github.com/eltmon/overdeck/pull/5166
- HEAD reviewed: e88c4b58e45da51aa25454de1690ff74ef2c3528
- Base / prior cycle SHA: merge-base 2e6d2c50e80 (main); no prior review cycle

## Blocking Findings

### [correctness] New circular import: agent-injection → launch-pack-mcp → launch → … → settings-api → agents → messaging → agent-injection — `src/lib/mcp/agent-injection.ts:110`
- Severity: ! MUST
- Classification / requirement scope: specification defect followed by the implementation; in_pr_scope. The PRD contradicts itself. WI-6 step 2 prescribes this exact edge: "`async function launchPackServers(...) { const { resolveLaunchPackMcpServers } = await import('../skill-overrides/launch-pack-mcp.js'); ...`" inside `agent-injection.ts`, and D-1 puts the seam in `agent-injection.ts`. NFR-5 says "No new import cycle (`npm run lint:circular` passes)". The code followed WI-6 literally, and that breaks NFR-5. It still blocks, because NFR-5 is explicit and the required CI lint job is red.
- Spec correction: WI-6 should say that `agent-injection.ts` must not reach `skill-overrides/` or `skill-packs/sources.ts` through any import, dynamic imports included, because madge counts them. The pack-server resolver must enter through an edge that does not close the `settings-api → agents → messaging → agent-injection` loop (see Fix).
- Trigger and changed-code connection: `launchPackServers` (agent-injection.ts lines 109-117) does `await import('../skill-overrides/launch-pack-mcp.js')`; `launch-pack-mcp.ts` line 8 statically imports `./launch.js`, which reaches `deft/launch.ts` → `skill-overrides/resolve.ts` → `catalog.ts` → `skill-packs/sources.ts` → `settings-api.ts` → `agents.ts` → `agents/messaging.ts` → back to `mcp/agent-injection.ts`. The repo's madge-based guard counts dynamic `import()` edges, so the lazy import does not break the cycle.
- Expected / observed / impact: expected `lint:circular` to pass; observed:
  ```
  ✖ new circular dependencies found — these must be removed, not baselined:
      src/lib/agents.ts > src/lib/agents/messaging.ts > src/lib/mcp/agent-injection.ts > src/lib/skill-overrides/launch-pack-mcp.ts > src/lib/skill-overrides/launch.ts > src/lib/deft/launch.ts > src/lib/skill-overrides/resolve.ts > src/lib/skill-overrides/catalog.ts > src/lib/skill-packs/sources.ts > src/lib/settings-api.ts
  ```
  CI job `lint-group (core)` (run 43253681045, job 131306058166) fails on this for the exact HEAD, so the PR cannot merge green.
- Evidence: reproduced locally with `npm run lint:circular` at HEAD e88c4b58e45 (same output, exit 1); CI log for job 131306058166 shows the same cycle as the only failure. Limitation: I did not test a specific fix.
- Fix: break the edge from `agent-injection.ts` into the skill-pack catalog graph. Any path from `agent-injection.ts` to `skill-packs/sources.ts` closes the loop through `settings-api.ts`, so swapping one module in the middle of the chain won't fix it. Options: (a) have launch call sites (or a small registration seam set at startup) supply the pack-server resolver to `prepareClaudeOverdeckMcp`/`prepareCodexOverdeckMcp`, so `agent-injection.ts` no longer imports `launch-pack-mcp.ts`; or (b) cut a different edge in the chain, for example the `sources.ts` → `settings-api.ts` dependency. The guard's message says new cycles must be removed, not baselined, so don't add the cycle to `scripts/circular-deps-baseline.txt`. Re-run `npm run lint:circular` to confirm.

## Non-blocking Findings

1. **~ Docs overstate what an unconsented pack shows** — `configuration/mcp.mdx` ("A pack you trusted before this consent model keeps saying its MCP servers are **Not applied** until you run `pan skills pack update <id>`"). Classification: implementation/docs mismatch, in_pr_scope. In `readPackManifest`, `capabilities.mcpServers` is now `mcp.notApplied > 0`, so a previously trusted claude-plugin pack whose only servers are https ones loses the "MCP servers" Not-applied label in `pan skills pack list` and on the dashboard. Its servers still do not reach agents (correct per D-4), and each launch warns. But the docs promise a label that is no longer shown. Fix: reword the doc to say the servers stay unapplied and each launch warns until `pan skills pack update <id>`. Or, if the label is meant to stay, keep `capabilities.mcpServers` true when servers are applied but not consented (that needs registry data at manifest time, so the doc change is simpler).
2. **~ `pan doctor` "off everywhere" misses per-skill and issue-level enablement** — `src/cli/commands/doctor-atlassian.ts:37`. Classification: spec gap (the code follows WI-7's `packOnSomewhere` definition). D-5 makes the server reach agents when any atlassian skill is on per skill (e.g. `atlassian/triage-issue: true` with no pack toggle), on an issue-level pack toggle, or in a conversation layer. The doctor only checks global and project pack toggles, so in those setups it reports `atlassian pack registered and off everywhere; endpoint not checked` while agents do get the server. The impact is a misleading doctor row, not a launch failure.
3. **≉ Codex skip warning hard-codes the `atlassian:` prefix** — `src/lib/mcp/agent-injection.ts:243`. `atlassianNeedsInteractiveAuth` matches any pack server at `https://mcp.atlassian.com`, so a non-atlassian pack declaring that URL would log `[pack-mcp] atlassian: …` under the wrong pack id. This is cosmetic, and only the atlassian pack declares that URL today.
4. **? Extra pack-catalog read per launch inside the dashboard process** — `prepareClaudeOverdeckMcp`/`prepareCodexOverdeckMcp` now call `resolveLaunchPackSelection` → `listPackCatalog` (it reads every registered pack's manifest from the cache) on each launch, in addition to the launcher's own mount pass. All I/O is async and bounded by the number of registered packs (a handful), so I don't expect material impact. A timing measurement on a host with gstack registered would settle it.
5. **≉ `warnUnprovisionedProjectServers` drops pack names when project resolution throws** — `agent-injection.ts:190`. The pack lookup is nested inside the project try block, so a project-resolution failure suppresses the whole warning. This is best-effort logging only.

### Dimensions
- **Correctness:** blocker 1 (import cycle). The consent, selection, precedence (overdeck → role → project → pack → lower pack id), and Codex D-7b skip logic match D-4 to D-8. updatePack re-prompts when the commit is unchanged but consent mismatches, and the preview then shows the `MCP servers` row.
- **Security:** pack servers need https, `type: http`, no `${`, and explicit consent, so a stdio server is never applied. The Basic header is attached only for pack id `atlassian` and only to `https:` with exact hostname `mcp.atlassian.com`; I checked that look-alike hosts and http are refused. The header is written only to the 0600 launch file (`writeLaunchMcpConfig`) or the per-agent Codex config. No warning or doctor row includes the token (tests cover this). The `--allowedTools` auto-approval of pack tools is D-8, an explicit spec decision.
- **Paths traced beyond the diff:** (a) remote (Fly) launches: `src/lib/remote/remote-agents.ts` builds its own launcher and never calls `prepareClaudeOverdeckMcp`/`prepareCodexOverdeckMcp`, so neither the pack server nor the Jira header reaches a remote VM. (b) ACP host: `src/lib/acp/mcp-config.ts` skips any entry whose `type` is not `stdio`, so `acp`/`opencode` get no pack server (non-goal 4 holds). (c) Codex: `src/lib/runtimes/codex.ts` renders http entries with `escapeTomlBasicString(url)` and `inlineTable(headers)`, so a pack-supplied url or header cannot break out of the TOML; the file is written 0600. (d) All four `writePackEntry` callers in `sources.ts` (addPack, updatePack, enablePackBrowser `{...entry, browser: true}`, disablePackBrowser) keep or set `mcp` correctly. (e) `addPack`/`updatePack` have only CLI callers (`src/cli/commands/skills.ts`), and that preview prints the `MCP servers` row, so `mcp: true` is recorded only after a preview that showed the servers. (f) `collectDoctorChecks` is CLI-only, so the Atlassian probe never runs on a dashboard poll.
- **Non-goals:** honored. Only `claude-plugin` packs yield `manifest.mcpServers`, since `readPackMcpServers` runs only for that adapter. stdio and sse entries are never applied, and `${` is rejected rather than expanded. ACP drops http entries. No OAuth driving or token storage. No fork used. No dashboard UI change. No release run.
- **Performance:** advisory 4 only; all new I/O is async (NFR-1 met; no execSync added).
- **Requirements/UX:** see the matrix below; advisories 1 and 2 are UX accuracy gaps.

| 8 (WI-8/9) docs, no em dash, `lint:docs` | met (with advisory 1) | docs present; no em dash in added lines; `npm run lint:docs` passed locally at HEAD |
| NFR-5 no new import cycle | **unmet** | blocker 1 |

- `npx vitest run src/cli/commands/__tests__/doctor-atlassian.test.ts src/lib/skill-overrides/__tests__/launch-pack-mcp.test.ts src/lib/skill-packs/__tests__/adapters.test.ts src/lib/skill-packs/__tests__/sources.test.ts tests/unit/lib/mcp/agent-injection.test.ts src/lib/skill-overrides/__tests__/launch.test.ts`: 6 files, 182 tests passed.
- `npm run lint:circular` at HEAD: **failed** (new cycle, blocker 1).
- CI for HEAD e88c4b58e45 (`gh pr checks 5166`, final re-check before signaling): `lint-group (core)` **fail** (the cycle), and the aggregate `lint` job **fail** (it follows core). All of these pass: test-shard 1/4 to 4/4 (the CI test job), test-e2e, the non-blocking flake lane, build (22), clean install + server smoke, lint-group (effect), lint-group (skills), lint-group (state), integrations, and the prompt-trailer gate. Mintlify was skipped.
- `overdeck/test` (the local verification gate) reported pass, but it does not cover `lint:circular`, so I do not cite it as lint evidence.
- `lint-group (core)` stops at its first failure, so I ran the core lints that follow `lint:circular` locally at HEAD: `lint:ratchet-audit`, `lint:quarantine-audit`, `lint:effect-facades`, `lint:docs` and `lint:last-verified` all passed. The core lints before `lint:circular` (eslint, file-size, source-introspection, and the rest) passed in the CI job. So the cycle is the only red lint.
- `npm run lint:effect-diagnostics` (local, HEAD): passed, "227 known findings; none new".
